draft.title: Christian environmental ethics
card: Many Christians believe God created the world and that creation has worth because God made it. Genesis presents creation as good.
the belief that people are caretakers of creation, not its owners. They are responsible to God for how they treat it.
Some Christians read the Genesis call to have dominion over creation as a call to care for it, not to use it without limit. Christians may read this passage in different ways.
This belief can lead Christians to act, for example by reducing waste, protecting habitats or backing action on climate change. Churches and individuals may respond in different ways.
draft.remember: Many Christians see creation as God's, so people are caretakers who answer to God for how they treat it.

a.q: Which statement best expresses the Christian idea of stewardship?
opts: People care for creation because it belongs to God
People own creation and may use it as they choose
People should leave creation alone and never touch it
People care for creation only because it helps humans
a.why: Stewardship means people look after creation on God's behalf, so they answer to God for how they treat it. The idea of ownership is tempting, but it is wrong because stewards are caretakers, not owners.
a.clue: A steward looks after something that belongs to someone else.

b.q: A parish in Bathurst starts a program to restore a local creek. The priest says, "This creek is part of God's creation, and we are answerable for it." Which belief does this show?
opts: Stewardship, because people are responsible for creation
Ownership, because people hold creation as their property
Dominion as a right to use creation without limit
Separation, because creation has no link to faith
b.why: The priest says the creek is God's and that people are answerable for it. That is stewardship, which links care for creation to responsibility before God. Dominion is tempting, but the card says many Christians read it as a call to care, not to use creation without limit.
b.clue: Whose creek does the priest say it is, and who is answerable?

a.best: People care for creation because it belongs to God

b.best: Stewardship, because people are responsible for creation

problems.detail: The why says 'the card says many Christians read it as a call to care', but the card says 'Some Christians' read dominion this way. The why misquotes the card and overstates how widely this reading is held.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, and each question has one clear right answer. The only problem is that why (b) misquotes the card, saying 'many' Christians read dominion as care where the card says 'some'.

flags: Question b, other: The why says 'the card says many Christians read it as a call to care', but the card says 'Some Christians' read dominion this way. The why misquotes the card and overstates how widely this reading is held.
